analysis.title: Public Service Enterprise Group (PEG): First Take: Slight miss vs GSe/Consensus; NJ regulatory clarity and growth opportunities remain
key_insights: PEG reported 3Q26 operating EPS of $1.15, a miss versus GS estimate of $1.18 and FactSet consensus of $1.19.
Company reiterated 2026 EPS guidance of $4.28-$4.40 (GSe $4.40) and its long-term 6%-8% EPS CAGR through 2030.
The $24-$28 billion five-year capital plan is maintained with no need for new equity or asset sales.

PSE&G remains on track for ~$4.2 billion of regulated capital investment in 2026 and expects to file a proposal with the NJBPU to address regulatory lag on capital investments since its last distribution rate case.
PSE&G's annual FERC transmission formula-rate update adds ~$60 million of annual transmission revenue effective January 1, 2027, subject to true-up.
NJBPU approved $14 million (IAP) and $8 million (CEF-EV) of annual revenue increases effective October 1. The Phase 2 NJBPU business model review report is expected in early 2027.

The quarterly variance came from lower gross profit and higher interest expense, partly offset by higher other income and lower taxes. PSE&G EPS was $1.01 vs GSe $1.10, while Power & Other was $0.14 vs GSe $0.08.
GS expects the call to focus on NJBPU Phase 2 and the upcoming base rate case filing, large-load outlook after FERC's RBP and IRAS decisions, and generation and nuclear opportunities.
GS is Neutral on PEG with a 12-month SOTP-based price target of $83, implying 11.7% upside from $74.29.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral rating and $83 SOTP-based target maintained after a slight 3Q26 miss. Regulatory clarity in NJ and capital plan growth opportunities remain.

sector_views.rationale: PEG is rated Neutral relative to the Americas utilities coverage universe, with NJ affordability-driven regulatory shifts cited as a key risk.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 operating EPS reported $1.15 vs GSe $1.18 and FactSet consensus $1.19 (miss).
Segment EPS reported: PSE&G $1.01 vs GSe $1.10 (-$0.09); Power & Other $0.14 vs GSe $0.08 (+$0.06).
Net income reported $574mn vs GSe $589mn (-3%); PSE&G $506mn vs GSe $550mn (-8%); Power & Other $68mn vs GSe $39mn (+75%).
Gross profit reported $1,895mn vs GSe $2,021mn; interest expense $280mn vs GSe $238mn; other income $337mn vs GSe $150mn; income tax expense $77mn vs GSe $110mn.
2026 EPS guidance reiterated at $4.28-$4.40 (GSe $4.40). GS forecasts: 4Q26E EPS $0.81 and 2027E EPS $4.71.
risk_factors: A data center contract could accelerate earnings at Power (upside).
Regulatory shifts in New Jersey due to customer bill affordability.
Potential upside to the current capital plan.
